title: Namibia
capsule: Namibia became independent on 21 March 1990 after a protracted liberation struggle against South African administration, which had held the territory as South West Africa under a League of Nations mandate (1920) and, after 1966, in defiance of UN resolutions. The South West Africa People's Organization (SWAPO) under Sam Nujoma had waged armed resistance since 1966; the New York Accords of December 1988 linked Namibian independence to the withdrawal of Cuban troops from Angola, enabling a UN-supervised transition. Nujoma became the country's first president and SWAPO won the constituent assembly elections in November 1989, with independence formally proclaimed the following March. Namibia encompasses the Namib and Kalahari deserts, is among the world's most sparsely populated countries, and holds major deposits of diamonds and uranium.
